title: Fuel-Efficient Driving & Emissions
whatItIs: Using less fuel cuts costs and harmful emissions. Don't leave the engine running unnecessarily, keep tyres correctly inflated and get emission control faults fixed quickly.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT leave an engine running unnecessarily while your vehicle is stationary on a public road.

keyFacts: Likely to be stopped for more than a couple of minutes? Apply the parking brake and switch off the engine.
A 20% drop in tyre pressure can increase fuel consumption by 2%.
SAFED, the DfT-approved Safe and Fuel Efficient Driving programme, has shown average fuel savings of over 10%.

keyFacts.text: Exhaust emissions MUST NOT exceed prescribed levels.

keyFacts: Watch the emission control warning lamps and keep the AdBlue (diesel exhaust fluid) level topped up.

visual.caption: What helps a lorry use less fuel

items.title: Engine off
items.text: Don't leave it running unnecessarily when stationary on a public road.

items.title: Tyres
items.text: Keep tyres correctly inflated. Energy efficient tyres also help.

items.title: Aerodynamics
items.text: Wind deflectors can reduce drag and fuel consumption.

a.label: Switch the engine off
points: Parked, or stationary for more than a couple of minutes
Apply the parking brake as well

onTheTest.question: You're parked on a public road and expect to wait 20 minutes to unload. What should you do?
options: Apply the parking brake and switch off the engine
Keep the engine idling to keep the cab warm
Rev the engine every few minutes
Leave the engine running with hazard lights on
onTheTest.why: Don't leave an engine running unnecessarily while stationary. Stopped for more than a couple of minutes? Parking brake on, engine off.

onTheTest.question: How can tyre pressure affect fuel use?
options: A 20% drop in pressure can raise fuel use by 2%
Lower pressure always reduces fuel use
Tyre pressure has no effect on fuel use
A 20% drop in pressure can raise fuel use by 20%
onTheTest.why: DVSA guidance: a 20% drop in tyre pressure can result in a 2% increase in fuel consumption. Correctly inflated tyres help reduce fuel use.

traps: Idling while stationary on a public road can be an offence, not just a waste of fuel.
Coasting (in neutral or with the clutch down) removes engine braking and reduces your control.
Modifying, removing or failing to maintain an emission control system can be an offence and risks the operator licence.
